   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, November 5, 2019

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Harrington
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Pu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Costanzo,
  Harrington, Liao

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. MOST BUSINESS FRIENDLY CITY IN LOS ANGELES COUNTY FINALIST
  B. INTRODUCTION OF RECREATION SUPERVISOR — MATTHEW MORALES-
  STEVENS
  C. INTRODUCTION OF PUBLIC WORKS MAINTENANCE WORKER I — STEVE
  MANCILLAS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. You
  will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 5, 2019  2
   The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of October 15, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of October 15, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT — SEPTEMBER 2019

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of September 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 657 AMENDING
  TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE — FINANCE
  AND REVENUE

  The proposed Ordinance will amend Title III, Section 34 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code by providing for the use of mechanical signatures on city issued
  checks, updating the purchasing procedures section to modify and clarify
  purchasing policies and procedures used to procure goods and services for City
  operations, and making minor modifications to the Informal Bidding
  Procedures for public projects. The majority of changes within the purchasing
  procedures code section were approved by Urgency Ordinance No. 656 on
  September 17, 2019 and are provided herein as to further ratify those
  provisions. The first reading of this proposed ordinance was conducted on
  October 15, 2019.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading, read by title only,
  and adopt at the Second reading, Ordinance No. 657 amending Title III, Section
  34 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, pertaining to Claims and Demands,
  Purchasing Procedures, and Informal Bidding Procedures.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 5, 2019  3
   E. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR GREAT STREETS PROGRAM
  CONSTRUCTION CITY CONTRACT NO. 19-08, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT NO. 1-08-35

  The Great Streets Program will construct pavement rehabilitation at several
  locations citywide. The annual Great Streets Program reconstructs and
  maintains the City’s pavement as identified through field investigations and the
  City’s Pavement Management Program. The Great Streets Program for 2019
  Phase 2 includes rehabilitation of pavement on Santa Anita Street between
  Mission Road and Mission Drive, Arroyo Drive between Santa Anita Street and
  Mays Alley, Carmelita Drive between San Marcos Street and Mission Drive,
  Junipero Place between Clary Avenue and Broadway, Clary Avenue between
  Junipero Place and Junipero Serra Drive, Alley West of City Hall, Bilton Way
  between Fairview Avenue and Orange Street, and Orange Street between
  Montecito Drive to Del Mar Avenue. Bilton Way and Orange Street were
  included as additive alternate bid schedules in the bid package, to be awarded
  if sufficient funds remained after the base bid.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the plans and specifications for the Great Streets Program, City
  Contract No. 19-08
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute contract documents with Sequel
  Contractors, Inc., for the bid amount of $2,236,520; and
  3. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $2,460,172 which includes a
  10% construction contingency and a $50,000 construction allowance to
  integrate fiber reinforcement into the asphalt.

  F. PURCHASE OF SEWER VIDEO INSPECTION TRUCK

  The Public Works Department is responsible for the operation and maintenance
  of the City’s sewer system which consist of 72 miles of sewer lines, 1350
  maintenance holes and one lift station. Maintenance consists of routine line
  cleaning by jet truck, daily inspections of the lift station, and video inspections
  as needed. The City is also required to video sewer lines every 5 years as a
  condition of the Consent Judgement. The video inspections are currently
  outsourced and the most recent contract for video inspection was completed
  in 2017 and exceeded $400,000. This video truck will enable the Public Works
  Department to video the sewer system with our own staff and comply with the
  requirements of the Consent Judgement at a much lower cost.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 5, 2019  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve purchase of the Sewer Video
  Inspection Truck from Haaker Equipment Company in the amount of
  $191,742.65.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 655 ADOPTION OF 2019 CALIFORNIA BUILDING AND
  FIRE CODES — INTRODUCTION

  The California Building Standards Commission has adopted new building and
  fire codes to take effect on January 1, 2020. Publications were available as of
  July of this year. The Building and Safety Division and Fire Department staff
  have monitored the development of these codes closely, and are engaging in
  training to ensure that the City’s building and safety and fire personnel are
  properly trained to implement the new standards. The implementation and
  enforcement of the most current building codes result in safer buildings and
  communities that suffer less damage when natural disasters occur.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive further reading, read by title only,
  and introduce for first reading Ordinance No. 655, adopting the following
  California Codes, and making related amendments to the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code:

  1. Adoption of California Administrative Code, 2019 Edition, and the State of
  California Title 24, Part 1, including Errata and Supplements hereafter;

  2. Adoption of California Building Code, Volumes 1 and 2, including Appendix
  Chapters A, C, H, I, and J, 2019 Edition, California Historical Building Code,
  including Appendix Chapter A, 2019 Edition, California Existing Building
  Code, including Appendix Chapter A1, 2019 Edition, and the State of
  California Title 24, Parts 2, 8, and 10, California Building Code Amendments
  of 2019, including Errata and Supplements hereafter;

  3. Adoption of the California Residential Code, including Appendix Chapters
  A-E, G, H, J, K, O, and P, 2019 Edition, and the State of California Title 24,
  Part 2.5, California Residential Code Amendments of 2019, including Errata
  and Supplements hereafter;

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 5, 2019  5
   4. Adoption of California Electrical Code, including Appendices A-I, 2019
  Edition, and the State of California Title 24, Part 3, California Electrical Code
  Amendments of 2019, including Errata and Supplements hereafter;

  5. Adoption of California Mechanical Code, including Appendix Chapters B-
  D, and F, 2019 Edition, and the State of California Title 24, Part 4, California
  Mechanical Code Amendments of 2019, including Errata and Supplements
  hereafter;

  6. Adoption of California Plumbing Code, including Appendix Chapters A-D,
  G, and H-K, 2019 Edition, and the State of California Title 24, Part 5,
  California Plumbing Code Amendments of 2019, including Errata and
  Supplements hereafter;

  7. Adoption of California Energy Code, including Appendix Chapters 1-A, 2019
  Edition, and the State of California Title 24, Part 6, California Energy Code
  Amendments of 2019, including Errata and Supplements hereafter;

  8. Adoption of California Fire Code, including Appendix Chapters 4, B, BB, C,
  CC, D-I, K, N, and O, 2019 Edition, and the State of California Title 24, Part 9,
  California Fire Code Amendments of 2019, including Errata and
  Supplements hereafter;

  9. Adoption of 2019 California Green Building Standards Code, 2019 Edition,
  and the State of California Title 24, Part 11, California Green Building
  Standards Amendments of 2019 including Errata and Supplements
  hereafter;

  10. Adoption of California Referenced Standards Code, 2019 Edition, and the
  State of California Title 24, Part 12, including Errata and Supplements
  hereafter; and

  11. Adoption of the additional administrative and miscellaneous revisions
  described on pages 3 and 4 of the staff report, and contained in the
  adopting ordinance.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. 2018-19 YEAR-END REVIEW (UNAUDITED), 2019-20 1ST QUARTER BUDGET
  REVIEW, 2020-21 BUDGET KICK-OFF

  This report summarized the City’s financial position for FY 2018-19 (unaudited)
  and FY 2019-20 through the first quarter ending September 30, 2019 for the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 5, 2019  6
   General Fund. Also included are carryover appropriations for capital
  improvement program and special/capital project funds, additional General
  Fund budget adjustments, proposed changes in staffing, and updates to the
  recently approved Citywide Fee Schedule. Lastly, the 2020-21 Budget Guiding
  Principles and Budget Preparation Calendar have been included as partial
  fulfillment of Fiscal Sustainability Policy requirements.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Receive and file the Fiscal Year 2018-19 Year-End Preliminary (unaudited)
  financial data and the 2019-20 First Quarter Budget Review Report;
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 19-56 amending the 2019-20 Operating budget for
  carry-over and miscellaneous appropriations in the Capital Improvement
  Program and Capital/Special Projects Funds;
  3. Approve recommended staffing changes by adopting Resolution
  No. 19-54 eliminating the vacant Revenue Collections Administrator
  position and adding a Revenue Services Specialist position and approving
  the revised salary schedule in accordance with CalPERS requirements;
  4. Approve the 2020-21 Guiding Principles and after review, receive and file
  the 2020-21 Budget Preparation Calendar;
  5. Authorize the City Manager to transfer General Fund contingency
  appropriations to departments affected by the pending legal settlement;
  and
  6. Provide direction on credit card fee pass-through to customer for both
  under and over $5,000.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 5, 2019  7
   The next Regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 19, 2019
  at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
  Gabriel, California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

   Discussion included the powers of the Joint Legislative Audit Comm ittee and
  details of state audits; a desire for less detail in future oral staff reports with a focus
  on changes since the last budget update; future sales of Proposition A funds;
  changes to the City's fees regarding use of credit cards for payment to ensure the

  the effect on City finances of San Gabriel's ballot measure passing or failing; and
  details of various line items in the report.

I  Following discussion, there was a consensus of the City Council that credit card
  fees should be passed on to users.

  Program and Capital/Special Projects Funds;

  and adding a Revenue Services Specialist position and approving the revised
  salary schedule in accordance with CalPERS requirements;

  recourse.

   work in January 2020, they are interviewing interim directors to take the City through

  recruitment for a Finance Director had not been successful as five local cities were
  recruiting for the same position at the same time. The City Council will be kept

I  which have benefited the City. He reported on the League of California Cities
